output.name: Hovan — The Nameless Lantern
output.myth: The boat went out past the Leeward rocks when Tavo came down on her like a dropped net. Her name was painted on the bow in red ochre. The sea took the ochre first, then the wood, and when the shore-folk found her ribs nobody could say what she had been called. My grandmother scraped what was left of the letters into a cloth and kept it in the lamp-box. A flake of paint is not a name, she said, only what the sea forgot to take. The lantern did not go out. It went up the mast of the sky and hangs low in the south, with Varesk the Cut Kite lying beyond it, still trailing the string Aun let go. Kael the Netter casts for it every night and hauls up only weed, and Tilsa the Net Shuttle, to its west, goes on mending the same holes. Hesk keeps count of it and will not write it down until someone gives it a name. So if you see it, do not call it lost. Say the name your mother gave you, and let the wind carry it.
output.finding: Find Tilsa, the Net Shuttle, then look a little under a hand-span to its east for a dim lamp with no name.
